_provenance.notes: Alaska seafood exports represent one of the most significant US agricultural export categories. Japan has historically been the #1 buyer of Alaska salmon roe (ikura, kazunoko) and high-value species. China processes a large share of Alaska pollock and salmon for re-export. Europe is growing as a premium wild salmon market. All values in USD millions.

annual_exports_by_country.notes: NOAA FEUS 1990. Japan dominant — salmon roe (ikura) and canned salmon. Japanese market pays premium for Alaskan quality.
NOAA FEUS 1995. Japan still dominant. China beginning as processor destination.
NOAA FEUS 2000. Collapse in export values — salmon price crash. Japan demand flat. Norwegian farmed competition hurts US exports.
NOAA FEUS 2005. China processing role growing rapidly — Alaska pollock surimi and salmon portions.
NOAA FEUS 2010. China becomes #2 destination — majority is processed/re-exported. EU premium market growing.
NOAA FEUS 2015. China now #1 by value — pollock processing + salmon fillets. ASMI 'Wild Alaska' brand growing in EU.
NOAA FEUS 2018. China processes ~60% of Alaska groundfish. Trade war Section 301 tariffs (25%) on Alaska seafood begin.
NOAA FEUS 2019. China tariff impact — 25% tariff on Alaska seafood. Chinese buyers shift volume. Some processing moves to Vietnam.
NOAA FEUS 2020. COVID disrupts foodservice globally. Retail demand compensates. Alaska exports hold up.
NOAA FEUS 2022. Record export year driven by record Bristol Bay harvest + high prices.
NOAA FEUS 2024 (preliminary). EU now strong #2 — premium wild salmon market. China processing sector stabilized post-tariff. Source: NOAA NMFS 2024 Fisheries of the United States.
